record.paper_title: The cosmological constant, dark matter, supersymmetry, and other unsolved problems from a fresh perspective
record.original_question: What new mechanism for CP violation can explain the prevalence of matter over antimatter in the current universe?

evidence.quote: Examples are the origin of Yukawa couplings, the origin of the Higgs boson mass, the nature of dark energy, an inflation-like mechanism in the early universe, a new mechanism for CP violation to explain the prevalence of matter over antimatter in the current universe

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the Standard Model of particle physics, the combined charge-conjugation and parity symmetry (CP) is violated in the quark sector through a single complex phase in the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa mixing matrix. The amount of CP violation predicted by this mechanism is known to be many orders of magnitude too small to account for the observed cosmological baryon asymmetry, i.e., the dominance of matter over antimatter in the present-day universe (with baryon-to-photon ratio of order 10^{-10}). Sakharov's conditions state that to dynamically generate such an asymmetry from a symmetric initial state one needs (i) baryon number violation, (ii) C and CP violation, and (iii) a departure from thermal equilibrium.

Problem: Propose and analyze a new mechanism of CP violation — beyond the Cabibbo–Kobayashi–Maskawa phase of the Standard Model — that, together with appropriate baryon-number-violating interactions and out-of-equilibrium dynamics in the early universe, quantitatively reproduces the observed matter–antimatter asymmetry of the present universe. Specify the underlying field-theoretic model, identify the new CP-violating phases or operators, and compute the resulting baryon-to-entropy ratio, demonstrating that it agrees with the observed value while remaining consistent with current experimental bounds (electric dipole moments, flavor-changing neutral currents, collider searches, etc.).
artifact.status_search_result: Generating the observed baryon asymmetry of the universe requires CP violation beyond that of the Standard Model, and identifying the actual mechanism (e.g., electroweak baryogenesis, leptogenesis, Affleck–Dine, etc.) is a long-standing open problem in particle physics and cosmology. No experimentally confirmed mechanism is currently known as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Baryogenesis review (Particle Data Group)
status_evidence.snippet: The origin of the matter–antimatter asymmetry of the universe remains unexplained within the Standard Model; CP violation in the CKM matrix is insufficient.
status_evidence.claim: The mechanism of CP violation responsible for the baryon asymmetry is unknown.
